source.publication: 2025 Schedule M1M Income Additions and Subtractions
source.section: Form M1 lines 1-4, 7-10 (instructions PDF p.13 Standard Deduction Table for Line 4, p.14 Worksheet A, p.39 Tax Rate Schedules, pp.32-38 tax table); Schedule M1M line 12 and Worksheet for line 12 steps 1-30 (M1M PDF p.3, p.4)

worked: Qualifying surviving spouse uses the joint amounts: AGI 110,000 is one step. Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages 93,000.00 + taxable Social Security 17,000.00 = 110,000.00. Social Security benefits (Form 1040 line 6a) 20,000.00; line 6b taxable 17,000.00 (federal worksheet: benefits taxable up to 85%; given, not tested). Federal taxable income = 110,000.00 - 33,100.00 federal standard deduction (31,500 plus 1 x 1,600) = 76,900.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form M1, qualifying surviving spouse: line 1 federal AGI 110,000.00. Schedule M1M line 1 other-state municipal interest 0.00; line 10 additions 0.00; Form M1 line 2 0.00; line 3 = 110,000.00. Schedule M1M line 12, Worksheet: step 1 110,000.00; step 2 108,320.00; step 3 1,680.00; step 4 1,680.00 / 4,000 rounded up = 1; step 5 0.1; step 6 17,000.00; step 7 1,700.00; step 8 = 15,300.00 (step 29, Tier 1 step 26 is 0.00). Keep share 0.9. Alternative method, projection: measure = federal AGI + tax-exempt interest = 110,000.00 + 0.00 = 110,000.00; cap first: lesser of 17,000.00 and 5,840.00 = 5,840.00; less 20% x (excess over 88,630.00, 21,370.00) = 4,274.00; alternative = 1,566.00. Worksheet steps 9-24 as printed: steps 9-11 110,000.00 - 17,000.00 = 93,000.00; steps 12-13 50% x 20,000.00 = 10,000.00; step 14 0.00; step 15 103,000.00; steps 16-18 0.00; step 19 103,000.00; step 20 88,630.00; step 21 14,370.00; step 22 2,874.00; step 23 5,840.00; step 24 2,966.00; step 25-27 17,000.00; step 28 2,966.00; step 30 greater of 2,966.00 and 15,300.00 = 15,300.00. Line 12 = the better of the two, 15,300.00. The projection's alternative entry loses, so only the simplified amount is applied. Schedule M1R: line 1 9,600.00; line 2 0.00 (65 or older); line 3 9,600.00; line 4 0.00; line 5 nontaxable Social Security 20,000.00 - 17,000.00 = 3,000.00; line 6 Railroad Retirement Board benefits 0.00; line 7 3,000.00; line 8 = 6,600.00. Line 9 110,000.00; line 10 14,500.00; line 11 95,500.00; line 12 47,750.00; line 13 = 0.00. Schedule M1M line 40 = Form M1 line 7 subtractions = 15,300.00 + 0.00 + 0.00 + 0.00 = 15,300.00 (lines 12, 16, 17, 25). State income before deduction = 110,000.00 - 15,300.00 = 94,700.00. Standard Deduction Table for Line 4 (PDF p.13): base 29,900.00 plus 1 x 1,550 age box(es) = 31,450.00; AGI is not over 238,950.00, so no Worksheet A. Line 4 = 31,450.00. Form M1 line 8 total = 31,450.00 + 15,300.00 = 46,750.00; line 9 Minnesota taxable income = 110,000.00 - 46,750.00 = 63,250.00. Line 10 tax from the rate schedule (PDF p.39): 5.35% x (47,620.00 - 0.00) = 2,547.67 + 6.80% x (63,250.00 - 47,620.00) = 1,062.84 = 3,610.51. The tax table (PDF pp.32-38) gives 3,611; expected keeps the schedule formula. Line 16 credits 0.00; state income tax 3,610.51.
accepted_approximations: Tax comes from the rate schedules at every income; below 86,800 of taxable income the booklet requires its 100-wide tax table.
